highlights: The pizza is baked in a traditional wood-fired oven at extremely high temperatures, often exceeding 450°C. This intense heat cooks the pizza in just 60–90 seconds, allowing the dough to rise quickly and develop its characteristic soft, airy texture. The result is a light crust with slightly charred edges and a delicate smoky flavor.

Neapolitan pizza originated in Naples, Italy, and over time became one of the most celebrated symbols of traditional Italian cuisine. Its history spans centuries and reflects the simplicity and authenticity of local culinary traditions. Today it is recognized worldwide as a cultural and gastronomic icon of Italy.

It is prepared using carefully selected ingredients — San Marzano tomatoes, fresh mozzarella, extra virgin olive oil, and fragrant basil. Each ingredient plays an essential role in creating the balanced, authentic flavor of the pizza. The focus is always on freshness, quality, and respect for traditional preparation methods.
